evidence.title: Dual backend object storage
evidence.normalized_claim: The application supports both local filesystem and S3-compatible object storage for exported documents.
evidence.description: The ObjectStorage protocol defines a common interface, and the implementation includes a LocalStorage class that stores files under a configurable root and a S3 backend (implied by the comment). Keys are backend‑independent and validated to prevent path traversal.

evidence.title: Deterministic signed URLs for downloads
evidence.normalized_claim: Downloads are served via signed URLs that expire after a configurable TTL.
evidence.description: The LocalStorage implementation generates HMAC signatures using a derived signing key and includes the key, expiration, and filename in the signature. The API endpoint `/api/v1/files/{key}` serves the file directly after verifying the signature.

evidence.title: Key validation logic
evidence.normalized_claim: The system validates storage keys against a regex and disallows traversal or empty segments.
evidence.description: The `validate_key` function checks the key against a compiled regex and rejects keys containing '..', '//' or failing the pattern, raising `InvalidKey`.

evidence.title: Evidence repository DTO boundary
evidence.normalized_claim: The worker layer interacts with evidence data through typed DTOs rather than raw ORM models.
evidence.description: `EvidenceRepository` defines `EvidenceCandidate`, `EvidenceHit`, and `EvidenceQuery` dataclasses, and the worker imports these instead of SQLAlchemy models, ensuring the worker does not depend on ORM internals.

evidence.title: Hybrid search configuration constants
evidence.normalized_claim: The repository defines constants for lexical, vector, and skill weighting and candidate limits used in hybrid evidence retrieval.
evidence.description: Constants such as `LEXICAL_WEIGHT`, `VECTOR_WEIGHT`, `SKILL_WEIGHT`, and `CANDIDATES_PER_SIGNAL` are declared at module level and referenced in queries.

evidence.title: Coverage computation actor
evidence.normalized_claim: Coverage calculation is performed by a Dramatiq actor that runs asynchronously and interacts with the database via SQLAlchemy sessions.
evidence.description: The `compute_coverage` function is a Dramatiq actor that schedules `_compute_coverage`, which opens an async SQLAlchemy session, loads a job, deletes old evidence matches, and performs hybrid search via the evidence repository.

evidence.title: Cancellation handling in coverage loop
evidence.normalized_claim: The coverage loop checks for cancellation before each LLM call and aborts if requested.
evidence.description: Inside `_compute_coverage`, before each requirement is processed, `is_cancelled(job_id_str)` is awaited; if true, the job status is set to cancelled, the session is committed, and the cancellation flag is cleared.

evidence.title: LLM reranking integration
evidence.normalized_claim: The coverage computation uses an LLM provider to rerank evidence hits.
evidence.description: The code imports `get_provider`, `get_embedding_provider`, and `config_for("rerank")`, and later calls `evidence_repo.hybrid_search` and passes results to an LLM rerank prompt (implied by imports of `PROMPT_VERSION`, `SYSTEM_PROMPT`, `build_user_message`).

evidence.title: Local ONNX embedding provider
evidence.normalized_claim: The project implements a local embedding provider using ONNX Runtime via fastembed
evidence.description: The `LocalEmbeddingProvider` class loads a BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 model with fastembed, caches the session per process, and applies a query instruction for BGE models. It exposes an async `embed` method that returns float vectors of dimension `EMBEDDING_DIMENSION`.

evidence.title: Retry logic with exponential backoff and jitter
evidence.normalized_claim: The project provides a retry wrapper that retries transient LLM provider failures with exponential backoff and jitter
evidence.description: The `with_retries` function in `retry.py` accepts an async operation, a retryable predicate, and retries up to `MAX_ATTEMPTS` with backoff calculated by `_backoff_delay`. It honors server-provided `Retry-After` headers and logs each retry attempt.

evidence.title: Groq provider using OpenAI SDK with structured JSON output
evidence.normalized_claim: The project implements a Groq LLM provider that uses the OpenAI Python SDK to send requests to Groq’s API and enforces strict JSON schema validation
evidence.description: `GroqProvider` constructs an `AsyncOpenAI` client pointing at `https://api.groq.com/openai/v1`. Its `structured_generate` method builds a system prompt that includes a JSON schema, sends the request, and expects a strictly validated JSON response. It also defines retryable error logic specific to Groq’s rate‑limit behavior.

evidence.title: Async FastAPI authentication API
evidence.normalized_claim: The repository implements an authentication API using FastAPI with asynchronous SQLAlchemy sessions and JWT-based token management.
evidence.description: The auth router defines endpoints for signup, login, token refresh, logout, and user info, all using FastAPI’s async capabilities and an AsyncSession from SQLAlchemy. Passwords are hashed with a dedicated hash_password function, and access/refresh tokens are created and validated via JWT utilities. Token revocation is handled through a revocation backend, ensuring refresh tokens cannot be replayed.

evidence.title: GitHub repository sync actor
evidence.normalized_claim: The repository contains a Dramatiq actor that synchronizes GitHub repositories, classifies files, scans for secrets, and updates source artifacts in a database.
evidence.description: The sync.py module defines an async function that runs as a Dramatiq actor. It fetches the default branch SHA, retrieves the repository tree, classifies each file, limits P2 priority files to 60, scans file contents for secrets, computes SHA-256 hashes, and compares against existing SourceArtifact records to perform idempotent updates. Events are published via a publish_event helper and telemetry is traced with traced_stage.
